title: Hydrogeochemistry of Coastal Shallow Groundwater for the Environmental and Health Risk Assessment: A Case of the Coastal Zone in the Quanzhou Bay
content:
Hydrochemistry in coastal groundwater in the Quanzhou Bay is predominantly governed by natural water–rock interactions. Agricultural non-point sources and domestic sewage contribute significantly to NO3 − contamination. Groundwater quality is generally classified as Class II to III, exhibiting a clear deterioration trend from inland to coastal areas. The NO3 − is identified as the predominant health risk contaminant, with children and infants being the most vulnerable populations.


ABSTRACT

To elucidate the hydrogeochemical characteristics and genesis of coastal groundwater under the combined influences of seawater intrusion and other environmental factors, 20 groundwater samples were collected from Quanzhou Bay during the 2023 wet season. An integrated approach combining hydrogeochemical analysis, positive matrix factorization (PMF), entropy-weighted water quality index (E-WQI), and a health risk assessment model was employed to investigate hydrochemical compositions, controlling factors, water quality, and associated health risks. The results identified carbonate weathering (18.6%) and seawater–freshwater mixing (32.6%) as the dominant hydrogeochemical processes. Elevated Na+ and Cl− concentrations in coastal areas indicated significant seawater intrusion, while high NO3 − concentrations reflected agricultural inputs and domestic sewage emissions. Overall, groundwater quality deteriorated progressively from the freshwater transect towards the bay transect. NO3 −-related health risks were more pronounced among children and infants. These findings provide a scientific basis for the sustainable management of coastal groundwater resources in southeastern China.
